title: Fresh unrest shuts garment factories in Bangladesh ahead of wage board meet
description:
Fresh labour unrest hit Bangladesh's garment industry on Sunday, with 13 factories shut indefinitely and five others declaring a one-day holiday, a day before the wage board is due to meet to continue consultations on recommending a revised pay structure.
Protesting workers gathered in Gazipur's Konabari and Mouchak areas, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them. Factory owners said 50 units in the industrial zone were closed.
The latest disruption comes amid weeks of protests over workers' demand to raise the minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka (USD 100) to 30,000 taka (USD 240), with demonstrations and factory shutdowns reported across key industrial belts.
Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80 per cent of the country's export earnings, making prolonged disruption a concern for international buyers and global supply chains.
